titles.li: On the trail of the herd

texts.li: [lowtech] Spear-carriers of {FACTION} came onto the colony's land this morning, bent low over a trail. Their leader, {X_nameDef}, straightened up long enough to tell {A_nameDef} that the herd they're after has stopped here, and that they'll camp {PLACE} until it moves on.

[!lowtech] A hunting party of {FACTION} walked in with rifles slung and a gutted carcass swinging from a pole between two of them. The hunting round here is the best they've had all season, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}. They'll camp {PLACE} until it thins out.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} crouched over a track not fifty paces from the colony, rubbed the dirt between finger and thumb, and said the game here was too good to pass up. The hunters with {X_objective} are already heading for a spot {PLACE} to make camp.

[winter] Snow drove the herds down off the high ground, and the hunters of {FACTION} came down after them. {X_nameDef}, stamping the cold out of {X_possessive} boots, told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} until the weather turns, and take no more than they need.

[fall] Fall is the hunting season, and a party of {FACTION} has followed the herds onto the colony's land. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, politely enough, where the colony would rather they didn't shoot, then chose a spot {PLACE} for their camp.

settled.li: The hunters from {FACTION} have their bedrolls down {PLACE}, a low fire going and a patch of ground cleared for dressing game.
[lowtech] A drying rack already stands beside the hunters' fire {PLACE}, with their spears leaning against it.
[!lowtech] The hunters of {FACTION} have pitched camp {PLACE}. They cleaned their rifles before they unrolled a single bedroll.
The hunters from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}, with a fire low enough not to spook the game and a lookout in the nearest tree.

joinTexts.li: "You eat better here than the trail ever fed me." {X_nameDef} from the hunters' camp has said it at the colony's table most nights this week, and tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether {X_pronoun} might stay.

Most evenings this week one of the hunters camped {PLACE} has turned up to help with the colony's butchering. Tonight {X_nameDef} lingered after the work was done, and asked whether there was a place for {X_objective} here.
{X_nameDef}, who tracks for the hunters camped {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} is tired of following the herds and would rather stay where the herds come to {X_objective}.

farewell.li: The herd moved on, and the hunters of {FACTION} went with it.
The hunters from {FACTION} rolled up their bedrolls, kicked earth over the fire {PLACE} and went off after fresh sign.
The hunters from {FACTION} were gone before dawn. All that's left {PLACE} is a ring of ash and a few cracked bones.
The hunters of {FACTION} broke camp at first light. One of them lifted a hand toward the colony from a long way off, and then they were over the rise and out of sight.

lines.li: Scrapes on that bark. Big one.
Whose turn is it to skin?

texts.li: A family of {FACTION} has come down the road with everything they own on their backs. Their home is gone, burned or taken, and {X_nameDef} would rather not say which. They ask only for a patch of ground {PLACE} to rest on for a while.

[lowtech] A handcart with one bad wheel has stopped at the edge of the colony's land, and a family of {FACTION} sat down beside it as if they couldn't push it another step. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether anyone would mind if they camped {PLACE} for a time.

[!lowtech] "A few days. A week at most." {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} said it twice to {A_nameDef}, as if the family behind {X_objective} needed to hear it too. They walked here with what they could carry, and would like to camp {PLACE} while they work out where to go next.

[ws:hunger] The farms in {FACTION}'s country stand empty after {SITUATION}, and one family of them has walked as far as the colony, thin as rails. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} until they know where they're going.

[ws:sickness] Every village on their road turned them away for fear of {SITUATION}. {X_nameDef}, of {FACTION}, swears none of the family is sick, and asks only to camp {PLACE} a while and keep to themselves.

[ws:war] {X_nameDef} doesn't know whether their house is still standing. When {SITUATION} came through the valley, this family of {FACTION} left with what would fit on a handcart, and they'd like to camp {PLACE} until it's safe to go back.

[ws:water] The water took their house in {SITUATION}, and a family of {FACTION} has walked up out of the valley with what they carried out of it. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a dry patch of ground {PLACE} to camp on.

[ws:drought] First the well went dry, then the fields. A family of {FACTION} held out through most of {SITUATION} before they gave up and took to the road, and {X_nameDef} has asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} for a while, near water.

[ws:weather] A family of {FACTION} came down out of the hills half frozen, driven out by {SITUATION}. {X_nameDef} could barely get the words out for the cold. They want a sheltered spot {PLACE} to camp until the worst of it passes.

[colony:Hospitable] A family of {FACTION} has come a long way on the word of strangers, who told them the colony takes people in and sends them on their way fed. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether it was true, and whether they might camp {PLACE} for a while.

settled.li: The family from {FACTION} has a windbreak up {PLACE} and their beds laid out close around the fire, the way people sleep after a long time sleeping rough.
[winter] The family from {FACTION} has dug their camp into the lee of a bank {PLACE}, with every blanket they own around the fire.
The family's camp is up {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} has already hung the washing out on the windbreak to dry.
The refugees' camp {PLACE} is small and tidy, their few things put away, and there's a cookpot on the fire with not much in it.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, from the family camped {PLACE}, came up to the colony this evening with a question {X_pronoun} had clearly been rehearsing. {X_nameDef} works hard, {X_pronoun} says, and would like to stay.

[ws:hunger|ws:sickness|ws:war|ws:water|ws:drought|ws:weather] {X_nameDef}, from the family camped {PLACE}, says there's nothing left to go back to after {SITUATION}, and asks whether the colony would take {X_objective} in.

{X_nameDef}, from the family camped {PLACE}, has been carrying water for the colony's cook in the evenings without being asked. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether there might be a place to stay for good.

farewell.li: The family from {FACTION} packed up their camp {PLACE} and went on down the road. {X_nameDef} waved until the colony was out of sight.
The family from {FACTION} found somewhere to go, or decided to look for it. Their camp {PLACE} is empty now.
[ws:hunger|ws:sickness|ws:war|ws:water|ws:drought|ws:weather] The family from {FACTION} packed up their camp {PLACE} to go and see what {SITUATION} has left of their home.
The family from {FACTION} has gone on. They left their camp {PLACE} swept, the fire ring raked out, as if they'd been guests in someone's house.

lines.li: Stay where I can see you.
Has anyone seen my other boot?

texts.li: A band of prospectors of {FACTION} has come onto the colony's land with picks, pans and a great deal of confidence. There's ore in this ground, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and they mean to camp {PLACE} until they find it.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} spread a map out on a flat rock for the colony to see: very old, much folded, with a cross inked close to where the colony stands. The prospectors of {FACTION} who came with {X_objective} mean to camp {PLACE} and dig until they find whatever the cross was for, and then sell it.

[!lowtech] Prospectors of {FACTION} have turned up with sample bags and a battered ground scanner, which {X_nameDef} thumped twice to show that it works. They plan to camp {PLACE} and dig test holes until they hit something.

[ws:rush] Everyone with a pan is out in the hills for {SITUATION}, and a band of {FACTION}'s prospectors has decided the colony's ground is worth a look. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE}, dig, and sell whatever turns up.

settled.li: The prospectors from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a windbreak against the weather and a torch to dig by after dark.
The prospectors' camp {PLACE} is up, and the first test holes are already dug in a neat line toward the high ground.
Sieves are stacked by the prospectors' fire {PLACE}, and a hand-drawn map is pinned flat under a rock beside them.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef} from the prospectors' camp is tired of digging holes for other people's fortunes, and asks whether the colony could use a steady pair of hands.
{X_nameDef} from the prospectors {PLACE} says the only thing worth finding round here is the colony, and asks, only half joking, whether there's a place for {X_objective} in it.
The colony's cook asked how the prospectors make their stew. {X_nameDef}, who makes it, would rather cook for people who stay in one place, and asks whether the colony could use a second cook.

farewell.li: The prospectors from {FACTION} filled in their last holes, packed up their camp {PLACE} and moved on, still sure the big find is over the next hill.
The prospectors from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} and left, arguing about where to dig next.
The prospectors from {FACTION} packed up {PLACE} and left, a little richer or a little poorer, depending on which of them you ask.

lines.li: There's a seam here, I can feel it.

texts.li: The pilgrims of {FACTION} who came limping up the road this morning have worn their sandals through. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, showed {A_nameDef} the holes, and asked whether they might camp {PLACE} a few days while they mend them.

They pray at dawn and at dusk, {X_nameDef} says, and in between they mostly sleep. The pilgrims of {FACTION} are bound for a holy place far beyond the colony, and would like to rest {PLACE} a few days on the way. They will take very little.

[ideology] Pilgrims of {IDEO} from {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land on their way to a shrine of their ideoligion. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to rest {PLACE} a few days, and to keep their prayers there.

[ideology,sameFaith] Pilgrims of {FACTION} who keep {IDEO}, the colony's own ideoligion, were glad to find it on their road. {X_nameDef} greeted {A_nameDef} in the words of their faith, and asked whether they might camp {PLACE} a few days before going on to the shrine.
[ws:faith] There are pilgrims on every road in the region for {SITUATION}, and a band of {FACTION}'s has stopped by the colony to rest. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' camp {PLACE}.

[winter] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have come through the snow on their way to a holy place, and stopped at the colony because they could go no further today. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} until the road clears.

[colony:Devout] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have turned off their road to rest at the colony. They'd heard on the way that it keeps its faith, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, and wanted to see that for themselves. They ask to camp {PLACE} a few days.

settled.li: The pilgrims from {FACTION} made a simple camp {PLACE}, with a place set aside for prayer.
[ideology] The pilgrims of {IDEO} have made their camp {PLACE}, with a shrine of piled stones at the edge of camp for their evening prayers.
The pilgrims from {FACTION} have laid out their sleeping places {PLACE} in a careful ring, and they sing before they eat.

joinTexts.li: The road has given {X_nameDef} what {X_pronoun} came for. Rather than walk on with the pilgrims camped {PLACE}, {X_pronoun} asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay with the colony.
[sameFaith] {X_nameDef}, one of the pilgrims {PLACE}, has found people of {X_possessive} own ideoligion at the colony, and asks to end the pilgrimage here.

{X_nameDef} has walked with the pilgrims {PLACE} since the first day of their road. Somewhere between the colony's gate and its table, {X_pronoun} says, it began to feel like arriving, and {X_pronoun} would like to stay.

farewell.li: The pilgrims from {FACTION} rested, prayed, and went on their way. {X_nameDef} said they'd remember the colony in their prayers.
The pilgrims from {FACTION} broke camp {PLACE} at dawn and walked on toward their holy place.
The pilgrims from {FACTION} left at first light, singing under their breath so as not to wake the colony.

lines.li: Mind your feet, they're all you have.
Bless the ones who let us rest.

texts.li: "Fair prices and honest weights," {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} was calling out, before the traders had even unpacked. They mean to keep a stall {PLACE} for a few days, and anyone with silver is welcome at it.

[lowtech] Peddlers of {FACTION} have stopped on the colony's land with full packs and a folding trestle. Market folk go where the buyers are, and this week that's here. They'll keep a stall {PLACE} for a few days.

[!lowtech] Traders of {FACTION} have arrived with packs, a folding table and a hand-painted sign that says OPEN on both sides. {X_nameDef} says they'll camp {PLACE} and keep the stall going for a few days.

[ws:trade|ws:road] With {SITUATION} bringing more traffic past the colony than ever, traders of {FACTION} have decided to stop and sell to it. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll put up a stall {PLACE} for a few days.

settled.li: The traders from {FACTION} have their stall up {PLACE}, with a torch to see the goods by.
The traders' stall {PLACE} is open for business, with the best of the goods at the front and a sign promising fair prices, which {A_nameDef} doubts.
The traders from {FACTION} have laid their goods out {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} is already calling prices to anyone in earshot.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who carries the traders' packs, has had enough of the road, and asks whether the colony would take on someone who can count and lift.
"Best market on the road," {X_nameDef} from the traders' stall {PLACE} keeps calling the colony, and tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether {X_pronoun} might stop moving and be part of it.
{X_nameDef}, who keeps the traders' accounts, has decided the colony needs someone who can tell a fair price from a bad one, and would like to be that someone.

farewell.li: The traders from {FACTION} folded their trestle and moved on to the next settlement.
Business was what it was. The traders from {FACTION} packed up their stall {PLACE} and left.
The traders from {FACTION} packed up their stall {PLACE}, counted their silver twice and went on, promising to be back when the roads are good.

lines.li: Fair prices, best on the road!
I'll throw in the bag for free.

texts.li: The cart came first, heavy enough to cut ruts, with helpers leaning into it from behind. {X_nameDef}, a traveling smith of {FACTION}, walked alongside and told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} a few days, sell what they've made and mend what they can.

[medieval] A smith of {FACTION} has stopped near the colony with an anvil on a cart and apprentices to push it. {X_nameDef} means to camp {PLACE}, burn some charcoal and sell blades and mail to anyone who can pay.

[industrial] {X_nameDef}, a smith of {FACTION}, travels with a portable forge on a handcart and a sack of coke. They'll camp {PLACE} a few days, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, fix whatever the colony brings them, and sell the rest.

[winter] A smith of {FACTION} has come in out of the cold, glad of an excuse to light a forge. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they'll camp {PLACE} until the weather turns, and mend whatever the winter has broken.

settled.li: The smith from {FACTION} has a work spot and a table of wares set up at the camp {PLACE}. The ringing of a hammer carries all the way to the colony.
The smith's camp {PLACE} is up and the forge is lit, and two colonists have already found reasons to walk past it with bent tools.
A fire burns hot at the smith's camp {PLACE}, and a row of half-finished blades lies cooling on a flat stone.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who has been working the smith's bellows, wants to stop moving, and asks whether the colony needs someone who knows metal.
{X_nameDef} from the smith's camp {PLACE} has been eyeing the colony's workshop for days, and finally asked whether {X_pronoun} might work in it, for good.
{X_nameDef}, the smith's apprentice, has been watching the colony's crafters work and thinks {X_pronoun} could learn more here than on the road. {X_nameDef} asks to stay.

farewell.li: The smith from {FACTION} loaded the cart and moved on, the anvil ringing faintly over every bump in the road.
The smith's camp {PLACE} is gone, and with it the hammering that ran from dawn to dusk.
The smith from {FACTION} put out the forge {PLACE}, packed the anvil and left a fixed hinge on the colony's gate without saying a word about it.

texts.li: "A season. Then I go." That was all {X_nameDef}, once of {FACTION}, would say to {A_nameDef} before going back to pacing out a spot for a hut {PLACE}.
{X_nameDef}, a hermit who left {FACTION} years ago, has chosen a spot {PLACE} to build a hut for the season. {X_nameDef} asks nothing of the colony and seems to hope the colony will ask nothing back.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, a hermit of {FACTION}, has come down out of the snow line, where even hermits can't stay in this weather. {X_nameDef} means to build a hut {PLACE} and wait the winter out, and would rather not be visited.

{X_nameDef} turned up {PLACE} with an axe, a sack and a blackened pot, and started cutting poles without asking anyone. When {A_nameDef} went over to see, {X_nameDef}, once of {FACTION}, said only that {X_pronoun} would be gone by the end of the season.

settled.li: {X_nameDef} finished a small hut {PLACE}, with a door, a roof and a fire outside it.
{X_nameDef}'s hut {PLACE} is finished: crooked, small and very solid. Smoke comes out of the roof in the mornings.
{X_nameDef} has a hut up {PLACE}, and a little garden fenced off beside it with sticks and twine.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, the hermit camped {PLACE}, came to the colony's door this evening. After a long silence, {X_pronoun} asked whether there might be room for one more.
For a week now there has been firewood stacked by the colony's door every morning. Today {X_nameDef}, the hermit {PLACE}, knocked, and asked to come in for good.
{X_nameDef}, the hermit {PLACE}, came to sit at the colony's fire one cold night and didn't leave when it burned down. In the morning {X_pronoun} asked to stay.

farewell.li: {X_nameDef} shut the door of the hut {PLACE} one last time and walked off without looking back. The hut is the colony's now, if it wants it.
The hermit's hut {PLACE} is empty. {X_nameDef} left in the night without a word, which is how {X_nameDef} arrived.
{X_nameDef} is gone from the hut {PLACE}. A little carved bird turned up by the colony's door the next morning, which may have been a goodbye.
